name: Author compliant components (privacy & compliance by construction)
desc: Build every component privacy- and compliance-safe from the start — data minimization, consent before non-essential, no dark patterns, secrets server-side — the author-time counterpart to the *-review skills.
body:
Author every component to be privacy- and compliance-safe BY CONSTRUCTION — the build-time counterpart to the `gdpr-review` / `hipaa-safeguards` / `pci-dss-review` / `soc2-readiness` review skills and the `audit-consent-scaffold` plumbing.
1. Data minimization: a component collects only what its purpose needs. Never add a field 'because we might use it later'. Don't capture or display PII (name, email, health, payment, precise location) without a clear, stated purpose.
2. Consent before non-essential: any component that captures data or triggers non-essential processing (analytics, marketing, tracking, third-party embeds) sits BEHIND the consent / preferences gate (see `audit-consent-scaffold`) — purpose-scoped, opt-in, withdrawable. Default to OFF.
3. No dark patterns: don't pre-check consent, don't hide or de-emphasize the decline, don't nag. Give accept and decline equal visual weight. Honor Do-Not-Track and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
4. Secrets & sensitive data stay server-side: never embed API keys, tokens, or secrets in a component; never log full PII / payment / health payloads client-side; mask sensitive fields (payment, SSN, secrets) in the UI.
5. Regulated categories carry stricter handling — flag them, don't hand-roll: health data (HIPAA), payment (PCI-DSS — never put raw card data in the component; use a tokenized/hosted field), and identity/behavioral data (GDPR). Route these through the compliant surface.
6. Auditability: a component that reads or mutates sensitive data surfaces through the audit-log choke-point (`audit-consent-scaffold`), never an ad-hoc write.
When building something that touches a regulated category, run the matching review skill (`gdpr-review` / `hipaa-safeguards` / `pci-dss-review`) against the result to confirm.
